newsitem.title: LEBANON: SVCD-Beirut Stock Exchange delists 38 companies.
newsitem.headline: SVCD-Beirut Stock Exchange delists 38 companies.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange delisted 38 companies that failed to meet listing requirements on time, chairman Gabriel Sehnaoui said on Monday.

"Due to the 12-month period expired on December 21, 1996 and because they had failed to meet the listing requirements, the BSE committee decided to cross out the companies that issued shares on the Beirut official market before December 21, 1995," he added in a circular.
The listing requirements cover issued capital and minimum number of shareholders.
The BSE re-opened in January after a 13-year closure during the 1975-90 civil war.

The companies named in the circular included Casino du Liban, electricity company Kadisha, Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, Credit Libanais bank, Banque Misr-Liban, Compagnie Libanais de Teleferique, Compagnie Libanais de Television, Almaza brewer, ABC stores and assurance firms Union Nationale and Libano-Suisse.

Sehnaoui said investors would be able to trade on the bourse's over-the-counter market the shares of any Lebanese stock company whose capital was equivalent of at least $100,000 after lodging an application and relevant documents.
The delisted companies could apply for listing once again, he added.
